claim_challenged: Capital before first revenue is $118k-$166k (L/W/T, base, excl. qualification) and the $1.0-1.5M Phase II pilot budget is revised to $133k
challenge: Capital stops at first invoice + 1 month of working capital, but the self-financing table shows the business losing money for years after first revenue (L -$270k at 1 customer, negative until 7; W/T negative until 16; C until 29). At one new customer per year the cumulative base-case deficit to sustained self-financing is L $1.06M, W $2.00M, T $2.24M, C $1.97M, F $0.31M (scratch run). Prior PRI-08 is defined as capital 'to the first referenceable paying customer... over 12-24 months' including build; the comparable excludes both build cash and post-revenue losses, so the claimed 85-90% reduction is not like-for-like. On a like-for-like basis the L figure (~$1.2M with qualification cash) confirms the prior instead of overturning it.
evidence: explore2.fsx: cumulative negative surplus over n=1..last-negative using evaluate baseSc n; self-financing.csv; prior-estimates.csv PRI-08 original_assumptions
proposed_change: Add a 'capital to self-financing' measure: sum of max(0, EfCash-Revenue) along a stated growth path (e.g. new_customer_share or 1/yr) until surplus stays >=0, plus qCash + readiness + WC; use it (not ExcludingQualification) as the PRI-08 comparable and in the s10 headline

claim_challenged: Break-even: L 7 customers, T 12, W 17, F 2 customers at 20 bps, F 7 at 10 bps
challenge: Counts are an artefact of the pattern order. Customer 7 in 'mixed' is the L profile (6,000 accounts, about half of all accounts in the 10-customer cycle) and customer 2 is an M profile (1,500 accounts, $270M AUA); every model's break-even lands on those positions. Same inputs with other mixes: small (all S) L 34, W/T never, F@10bps never, F@20bps 6; tiny: all never; anchor: L 2, F@20bps 1, F@10bps 1. At n=7 'mixed' carries 1,423 accounts/customer vs the cycle mean 1,182, so the reported counts are biased low.
evidence: explore.fsx BE runs per mix (cashFirst/sustained/loaded); mixes.csv pattern S M S XS M S L S M XS
proposed_change: Report break-even primarily in accounts and AUA (portfolio scale) and as a count only for (a) the expected customer (cycle-average profile, fractional) and (b) the min/max over rotations of the pattern; show all mixes side by side in s7 rather than 'mixed' only

claim_challenged: T cash break-even at 12 customers (reference price)
challenge: firstWhere returns the first n where revenue >= cost, not the point after which it stays there. T crosses at 12 then falls back below cost (step hires) and is only sustained from 17. Self-financing shows the same non-monotonicity (T surplus -$758 at 9, -$52k at 10).
evidence: explore.fsx: mixed T cashFirst=12 sustained30=17; self-financing.csv T row
proposed_change: Define break-even as the smallest n such that rev>=cost for all k in [n, n+30] (or to scanLimit); report both first-crossing and sustained

target: Analysis.fs:16-28 (headline uses atLevel Base); Sampling.fs:10-15; results.md s1/s13
claim_challenged: Headline tables at 'base' are the central estimate
challenge: Base is the mode of right-skewed triangular ranges (e.g. PLT-10 30k/48k/72k min, SEC-04 7k/12k/45k), so base sits below the independent Monte Carlo P10: L first-customer cash base $306k vs P10 $329k / P50 $373k; F $432k vs P10 $468k / P50 $517k; L zero-customer $44.6k vs P50 $70k. Mean-of-range inputs give L1 $384k, F10 $1.45M vs $1.17M (+24%). First employee: base 4 customers for L, but 68% of draws hire an engineer with the first customer (9% at zero customers). Calling these figures 'base' overstates confidence.
evidence: monte-carlo.csv vs headline.csv; explore2.fsx mean-input realisation and MC share of employees at n=1 (L 0.68, F 0.68)
proposed_change: Headline P50 (or the mean-input case) next to base and state the percentile of the base case; or re-centre ranges so base = median. Reword the staffing-threshold text to 'first employee at 1 customer in most draws'

claim_challenged: Steady-state cost at 1-2 customers and single-customer break-even AUA
challenge: max 1.0 (round(n*0.3)) puts a full new-customer onboarding into every year at n=1..4 (implementation 300-360 h, contract counsel $5k, 160 founder sales hours displacing contract engineering). At n=1 that is $58.8k/yr of L's $306k (19%) and F's $432k (14%); at n=2 it is $26.5k more than the fractional 0.6. A single customer cannot be both steady state and onboarding a new customer every year. Single-customer break-even AUA carries the same $58.8k (about $29M of AUA at 20 bps).
evidence: explore.fsx steady-state: L n=1 306,035 vs 247,235 with NewCustomers=0; n=2 321,288 vs 294,768 at 0.6
proposed_change: Split year-1 and steady state: steady-state tables use NewCustomers = n*new_customer_share (fractional, no floor); onboarding of customer 1 goes into capital/readiness (see ADV-A-08); the self-financing table can keep growth onboarding explicitly as 'growth cost'

claim_challenged: Labour cash is minimised given founder capacity
challenge: The founder takes min(hours, cap) of each role in register order even when coverage or the hire threshold forces employees whose capacity is then idle; freed founder hours are never moved to later roles (implementation, compliance, operations), so idle employees and paid contractors coexist. The coverage optimiser inherits this and undervalues the hire option. Patch (founder takes only hours not absorbed by forced employees) lowers cash by: T1 -$51k (-12%), F1 -$51k, L5 -$51k (-13%), W10 -$58k, L1 -$12k.
evidence: model-p1 patch: fh = min fh0 (max 0 (hours - minEmployees*ProductiveHours)); FOUNDER_ANY=1 run: L5 349,394 vs 400,140; F1 381,332 vs 431,930; W10 444,392 vs 501,970
proposed_change: Allocate founder hours after employee capacity (or solve founder allocation across roles to minimise contract+hire cost, e.g. greedy by contract rate avoided); re-run coverage choice on the reallocated staffing

claim_challenged: Coverage shortfalls are correctly netted against people already present
challenge: The founder counts as one distinct qualified person in every founder-eligible role at once (management, engineering, operations, compliance) even with zero hours in that role. At F1/T1 the founder's 1,400 h are used up by management and engineering (founder fully utilised at 0 customers), yet the founder is counted as one of the two people for COV-OPS business-day continuity and preparer/reviewer separation. Counting the founder only where they hold hours (on top of ADV-A-06) raises F1/T1 by about $40k (COV-OPS alternative $80k instead of $40k). It also lets one person be on-call primary, change approver, ops preparer and account manager at the same time.
evidence: model-p1 patch (fhRole>0 condition): F1 421,332 vs 381,332 with founder counted everywhere; F n=1 founder hours in operations = 0 in base run
proposed_change: Count the founder toward at most one coverage requirement set (choose the cheapest role to apply them to) and only where the founder holds >= a minimum share of that role's hours; add a Validate rule that founder coverage needs founder hours > 0

claim_challenged: Readiness = prepaid annual items newly triggered by customer 1; pre-revenue burn = months x zero-customer cost
challenge: Before the first invoice the business also pays for: first-customer onboarding (ACT-IMP-01 300 h L / 360 h F at $110 = $33-40k), contract counsel (EXP-COR-03 $5k), founder sales time (160 h, displacing about $21k of contract engineering, since the founder is already fully used at 0 customers), and coverage retainers that must exist once customer data is in production (COV-CHG/BRK/ONC $100k/yr, COV-OPS $40k). o0 contains none of these, and readiness counts only Prepaid=Y lines. Under this definition pre-revenue capital is understated by $60-100k+ per model.
evidence: Engine evaluate L n=1 role breakdown (implementation 300 h contract $33k; coverage $100k); capital.csv L base readiness $48.1k = SEC-03/04/05 + INS-01/02/07 only
proposed_change: readiness = (o1 cash - o0 cash for non-recurring onboarding lines and activities) + prepaid lines + go-live share of coverage retainers; or model the pre-revenue months with o1 staffing for the last k months before go-live

claim_challenged: Revised variable cost per account $98 (vs Phase II $147)
challenge: The comparable is (F at 5x2000 - F at 0)/10,000 accounts, so it includes every first-customer step cost (SOC 1/SOC 2 audits, GRC platform, insurance, coverage retainers, monthly-close and auditor-support hours per customer). That is average incremental cost, not variable cost. The actual per-account slope is $65 (1->5x2000), $46 (5->10) and $69 (10->20). The 'revised' variable figure is overstated, which makes the AI-native variable advantage look smaller than the model implies.
proposed_change: Use the slope (F(10)-F(5))/(accounts10-accounts5) or a regression over 5..20 x2000; keep the current figure but label it 'average incremental incl. first-customer step costs'

claim_challenged: $2.5M administration fixed revised to $1.03M; $1.8M licensing fixed revised to $405k
challenge: Scope mismatch: the priors are fixed costs only, but the comparables are total EF cash at 5x2000 including volume-driven labour. Like-for-like is total vs total (prior F $2.5M + $147 x 10,000 = $3.97M vs $1.03M, a 74% cut rather than 59%; prior L $1.8M + $31 x 10,000 = $2.11M vs $405k) or fixed vs fixed (intercept of the zero-based cost line). The table also drops founder labour from 'cash' while the priors priced a salaried CEO/CTO, so only the loaded rows are comparable on management.
evidence: results.md s12; Phase II report 10 ($397 vs $147 vs $31 variable)
proposed_change: Add a 'prior total at 10k accounts' column (fixed + variable x accounts) and compare against EfCash and FullyLoaded; or compare the priors' fixed against the zero-based intercept from a 5->10x2000 regression

claim_challenged: Customer acquisition cost revised from $125k to $24.7k
challenge: (a) EXP-ACQ-01 travel/procurement is tier 3, so it never applies at tier 1 and lineSum 'acquisition' is $0. (b) 160 founder hours are per won customer, with no win rate: at a 25-33% enterprise win rate, lost pursuits triple or quadruple founder time. (c) No marketing, conferences, security-questionnaire engineering hours or pilot concessions. (d) Founder time is priced at $123/h, not the management replacement rate ($144 loaded / $150 contract). A 25% win rate alone gives about $85k.
evidence: explore2.fsx L10 acquisition lines: only EXP-COR-03 $15,000 / 3 new customers; parameters.csv founder_hours_per_new_customer
proposed_change: Reclassify EXP-ACQ-01 as contract-typical (procurement travel is needed to win institutional deals); add param win_rate (0.2/0.33/0.5) dividing founder sales hours and counsel; add security-questionnaire engineering hours per pursuit

claim_challenged: Registry cost revised from $90-170k to $70.9k
challenge: The comparable omits ACT-PLT-09 'Charity and sanctions data pipeline stewardship' (200 h engineering, about $26k at $130/h), which is the connector maintenance the prior explicitly included (400 h), and omits ACT-SAN-01 sanctions triage. It also prices CHV hours at the founder rate instead of the compliance contract/loaded rate. Adding PLT-09 alone gives about $97k, inside the prior range, so the 'lower than prior' conclusion does not hold.
evidence: explore2.fsx PLT-09 h=200 at F 5x2000; prior-estimates.csv PRI-04 original_assumptions
proposed_change: registry = charity-data lines + (ACT-CHV-* + ACT-SAN-01) hours x compliance contract rate + ACT-PLT-09 hours x engineering contract rate (+ QUAL-03 amortisation in the loaded view)

target: Engine.fs:391-393 (SponsorCost); activities.csv sponsor rows; parameters.csv sponsor_staff_rate
claim_challenged: Sponsor-borne cost is reported completely and separately
challenge: Missing sponsor costs: sponsor-side onboarding and migration (data extraction from the incumbent, UAT, parallel run, staff training; ACT-IMP-01 is EF-only and there is no sponsor counterpart), incumbent exit/termination fees, the incremental external financial-audit fee (only staff hours in ACT-AUD-01), and review of SOC reports. sponsor_staff_rate $65/h (Phase II ops rate) is applied to controllers and authorised officers (REC-03 sign-off, GRT-02 decisions, OFAC blocking, AUD-01), who cost $90-150/h loaded. F_system_per_account and the L/W sponsor value proposition (sponsor does exception prep at $65 vs EF ops at $85) are understated.
evidence: headline.csv sponsor_cost (F1 $15.8k, L1 $41.3k); activities.csv has no sponsor onboarding activity
proposed_change: Add sponsor activities ACT-IMP-S (per_new_customer, 200-600 h) and an exit-fee expense; split sponsor rate into sponsor_staff_rate and sponsor_officer_rate ($90/$120/$160) keyed by activity

claim_challenged: Employees are hired once residual hours exceed 800 because an employee is 'cheaper and more reliable'
challenge: 800 h is far below the cost-neutral point (loaded / contract hourly): engineering 1,512 h, management 1,533, operations 1,423, support 1,303, implementation 1,273, compliance 1,061. Hiring at 801 h costs $196.5k against $104k of contract engineering. With cost-neutral thresholds: L10 -$41k (-8%), L25 -$82k, T5 -$41k, F25 -$77k. If reliability is the reason, it should be stated as a policy premium, not as cheapness.
evidence: hire.fsx with roles thresholds set to loaded/hourly: L10 480,365 vs 521,365; L25 998,039 vs 1,076,316
proposed_change: Set hire_threshold_hours = LoadedAnnual/ContractHourly per role (or make the reliability premium an explicit parameter) and correct the roles.csv wording

claim_challenged: Fully loaded C and M include amortised qualification
challenge: The whole DAF platform qualification (ledger, grant lifecycle, sponsor experiences, SOC 2 readiness; 8,360 founder h incl. VAL) is amortised into charity intelligence (C) and migration services (M) as stand-alone businesses: about $232k/yr, so C is $419k loaded at 0 subscribers and M $273k at 0 projects, and C's loaded break-even is 114 subscribers. C needs roughly QUAL-03 + part of QUAL-05. qualAmort also includes VAL-01/02 while capital's qCash excludes them, which is inconsistent.
evidence: results.md s2 C/M at 0 customers; qualification.csv
proposed_change: Add a models column to qualification.csv and amortise only applicable items per model; treat VAL consistently (either in both qCash and qualAmort or in neither)

claim_challenged: Monte Carlo with 'rho=0.5 adverse-correlated' inputs
challenge: The mixture copula (with probability rho take the common quantile) gives pairwise correlation of about rho^2, measured at 0.28 for rho=0.5, so the label overstates the correlation tested. The MC also holds volumes, mix and prices at base, so the narrow P10-P90 for 'F cash break-even bps at 10' (7.6-9.7) leaves out the mix uncertainty that dominates break-even (ADV-A-02).
evidence: explore2.fsx pairwise corr at rho=0.5: 0.280
proposed_change: Use p = sqrt(rho) for the mixture (or a Gaussian copula with the stated rho) and label as such; add volume factors and a random mix rotation to the MC draws

claim_challenged: Low/high columns in capital and prior tables are 'all favourable'/'all adverse' ranges
challenge: These are joint-extreme corners of about 300 ranges set at once (e.g. L capital $76.7k-$1.31M; PRI-01 $206k-$3.65M), with near-zero probability, shown as if they were ranges. The orientation also misses PAR:qualification_amortization_years (high is favourable for loaded, so 'adverse' uses 7 years and lowers loaded cost) and the loaded effect of founder_hours_per_year (1,900 h raises founder noncash in the 'favourable' case).
evidence: Engine.fs:16-18 list; capital.csv low/high rows
proposed_change: Replace oriented corners with MC P10/P90 of the same metrics; add qualification_amortization_years to lowIsAdverse

target: coverage.csv COV-BRK alt_description; Engine.fs:291 (alternatives priced independently)
claim_challenged: Coverage alternatives are additive and do not overlap with workload contractors
challenge: COV-BRK's own description says the second break-glass holder 'can be the secondary on-call', yet $12k BRK and $36k ONC are both charged. Contracted engineers already paid for 619-1,259 h/yr at L1-L2 are distinct qualified people who could serve as non-author reviewer or secondary on-call, but $100k/yr of retainers (a third of L1 cash) is added on top.
evidence: results.md s4 L1: 1,124 contract hours plus COV-CHG $52k, BRK $12k, ONC $36k
proposed_change: Allow one alternative to satisfy several requirements (a set-cover across alternatives: ONC retainer satisfies BRK); credit a contracted engineer with >= X h/yr as one person toward CHG/ONC

target: expenses.csv EXP-SEC-01/02/03, EXP-SUP-01 (fixed); no recruiting/equipment/financial-audit lines
claim_challenged: Expense register is complete
challenge: Headcount-driven costs are missing: seat-priced tools (workspace/identity, code hosting, GRC priced by FTE band, help-desk seats) stay fixed at 0 to 70 employees; there is nothing for recruiting fees (15-25% of salary per hire), equipment or contractor management. There is no financial-statement audit, although AUD-24 ($7k-$50k) is priced in the evidence file and bank-grade sponsors usually ask for vendor financials.
evidence: expense register drivers; data/evidence/prices-ops.csv AUD-24
proposed_change: Add per-employee tooling (Step on employees, needs an Employees metric), recruiting per hire, and EXP-COR-06 financial audit (contract-typical, from 1 customer)

claim_challenged: Insurance $9.6k/yr at tier 1
challenge: Prices come from micro-SaaS medians (Insureon customers mostly under 5 employees with $50-200k revenue). Underwriting for a vendor that originates payment instructions over $60M-$1.4B of charitable assets (crime/social-engineering, E&O for fund-accounting errors) is likely to be several times higher, and limits of $1-2M are low against a single misdirected grant batch.
evidence: prices-ops.csv INS-01 notes
proposed_change: Widen high ends (e.g. E&O/cyber $10-25k, crime $5-15k) or mark as ASSUMPTION pending broker indication; add a limit-adequacy check versus the largest payment batch

claim_challenged: Break-even prices per customer and per account; marginal $/customer
challenge: Per-customer and per-account floors are average cost of the specific mix at n (S, then S+M...), so the n=1-2 floors mostly reflect the S/M identities and perpetual onboarding (ADV-A-05). The 'marginal per customer' column is the cost of whichever profile is next in the pattern plus integer rounding of new customers (Math.Round uses banker's rounding: 1.5->2, 2.5->2, 4.5->4, 7.5->8), so L swings $3.5k / $15.3k / $101k. These are not usable as price guidance.
evidence: price-floors.csv L marginal column; Engine.fs:107
proposed_change: Compute floors on the expected (cycle-average) customer; use average incremental cost over bands (10->25, 25->50) for 'marginal'; use MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero or fractional new customers

claim_challenged: Presentation and units
challenge: Break-even AUA renders as '$1449.00M' / '$20067.00M' (no billions unit). 'never (≤400)' is printed for thresholds searched only to 200. The 'exceptions' metric equals transactions x exception-rate multiplier (2,880 'exceptions' on 2,400 transactions at L1), which reads as an exception count.
evidence: results.md s5/s7; headline.csv L1 row
proposed_change: Add a B unit to money; pass the actual scan limit to optInt; rename the metric to exception_weighted_transactions

claim_challenged: Cash break-even L 7 customers; cash cost is what EF must fund
challenge: The cash view assumes the founder works 1,400 h/yr on the DAF business indefinitely with no draw (noncash $172k/yr, constant at every count). The loaded view adds that but also adds qualification amortisation, so neither view answers 'when can the business pay its founder'. Adding a founder market salary moves L cash break-even from 7 to 8 and widens every pre-break-even deficit by $172k/yr (which also feeds ADV-A-01).
evidence: self-financing.csv L: +$154.6k at 7, +$187k at 8; founder_noncash 172,200 in headline.csv
proposed_change: Add a third view 'cash incl. founder compensation' (EfCash + founder hours x rate) for break-even, self-financing and capital

claim_challenged: Working capital = collection lag x monthly cost at 1 customer
challenge: Working capital is driven by receivables (lag x monthly revenue), with any shortfall in cost covered by the deficit measure, not by lag x cost. Using o1.EfCash also counts the prepaid annual items already in readiness a second time (about $4k for L). The deficit is not funded anywhere (ADV-A-01), so the WC line is not the binding item.
evidence: capital.csv L base wc $25.5k = 1 x 306k/12
proposed_change: wc = lag x Revenue(1)/12; fund operating losses separately; exclude prepaid lines from the monthly base

claim_challenged: Founder labour valued at market rate (fully loaded)
challenge: $123/h is the loaded developer rate (equal to engineering $196.5k/1,600 h), but the founder's first 490-530 h/yr go to management, where the replacement cost is $144/h loaded or $150/h contract. Qualification hours (ledger and fund-accounting design) are also priced at the developer rate. This understates fully loaded cost by about $10-15k/yr, plus the qualification loaded figure.
evidence: roles.csv management loaded 230,000 / 1,600 h; parameters.csv founder_imputed_rate basis
proposed_change: Value founder hours at the replacement rate of the role they fill (role LoadedAnnual/ProductiveHours) rather than a single rate
